criteria.build_driving_ops: Build the missing execution substrate before porting anything: Can operations that launch and supervise a real Chromium, speak CDP for navigation, clicking, script evaluation, cookie-store inspection, and CSP-violation capture, plus a test-only HTTPS client that tolerates self-signed certificates. Qualify and document that substrate, then migrate C02/C03 completely with every leg live and no blocked entries, and delete all four runners. Browser-queue progress gates on substrate delivery.
criteria.defer_browser_queues: Park the whole browser queue: keep the 2 .mjs runners, the 3 S03/S04 sources and document, and the 5 C04 fixture files exactly as they are, complete the remaining 6 non-browser records, and revisit C02/C03/C04 only when new observations or a new capability change the picture. No partial ports, no blocked-leg bookkeeping, no new runtime work; the checklist closes everywhere else first.
criteria.port_wire_with_blocked: Migrate what the wire already reveals: serve staged production routes in-process, drive them with fetch_bytes, judge with SQL descriptors, take S04 in full, run TLS-incidental assertions over plain HTTP, and approximate the single-use race sequentially. Re-point C02/C03 at the C01 fixture producer, delete the 5 C04 originals, and write the Chromium-enforced and TLS-listener assertions up as blocked legs that name their absent primitives. Keep the .mjs/.ts runners for those blocked legs only; add no runtime surface.

browser_scope.instructions: How should the migration handle the C02/C03/C04 browser queues so all 28 records end honestly disposed without orphaning retained behavior?

state.baselines: The browser queues hold four harnesses: proof.mjs under tests/site_delivery (171 lines, 9 PASS groups; Playwright driving Chromium against a self-signed openssl listener), strict-redirect.mjs under tests/site_delivery (90 lines), probe.ts under tests/site_preview for S03 (279 lines combining Can issuance, SQLite, HTTPS, and browser legs), and approval_probe.ts under tests/site_preview for S04 (168 lines of plain HTTP, SQLite, and file staging with neither browser nor TLS). The C01 fixture producer is finished; the C04 step deletes 5 fixture files once C02/C03 consume the producer.
state.browser_only_legs: These assertions have no Can-side execution path: running page JavaScript and reading live DOM/CSS/font/media outcomes (fixtureReady flags, getComputedStyle, fonts.ready, decoded-image dimensions, synthetic clicks), a genuine cookie store (__Host- scoping, HttpOnly, SameSite, redirect-time carriage, tamper rejection), browser-side CSP trip reporting (securitypolicyviolation), address-bar navigation with default and overridden referrer behavior, and worker plus serviceworker admission control. Roughly 5 of proof.mjs's 9 groups depend on them, as do strict-redirect.mjs's form-action refusal and click-chain cookie legs and the probe.ts lines 227-277 closer (2 groups).
state.mandate: Can exists to be written by AI coding agents; keeping old syntax, artifacts, or harnesses working is explicitly not required, and the operating rule ranks arriving at the goal above producing scaffolding or layered proofs. The migration tracks precisely 28 baseline records under manolea-2/tests, each retiring only after its kept legs succeed as executing Can verdicts over real production behavior, reconciled by F01. The host is a 256 GB laptop where free disk and load ceiling are binding limits.
state.mechanism_inventory: 44 browser:: catalogue entries implement DOM emulation inside the process (mounting, querying, events, state), and none of the 44 touches navigation, cookie storage, network dispatch, TLS, CDP, or outside-browser command (established by grepping the catalogue). The http::fetch_bytes operation, qualified 2026-10-02 with a 13/13 live run, handles plain-HTTP wire assertions with repeated ?query keys and hand-driven redirects. The 12 fulfilled records used exactly these mechanisms; browser driving has not been required by any finished port.
state.portable_legs: The bulk of the assertions travel over the wire and fit the established in-process recipe (production site_routes staged and served with server_start/stop, an http::fetch_bytes driver, probe-owned SQL descriptors, DDL through /usr/bin/sqlite3): grant issuance and claim with 303 chains, set-cookie strings off the wire, header bodies for CSP, referrer-policy, and cache-control, status codes, SQLite rows for grants, expiry, revocation, and maker state, byte-level file checks, and restart survival. S04 ports wholesale subject to one mounting choice (its exchange() invokes the TypeScript createPreviewHandler directly; the Can rewrite needs a matching Can production preview route, whose existence is still unconfirmed). The S03 Promise.all one-shot race ports as back-to-back claims proving second-claim denial, with simultaneity left as an explicit blocked leg.
state.tls_position: TLS terminates on the server side already (http::server_start_tls), but the test client cannot complete a handshake with the harnesses' self-signed fixtures: Bun's fetch aborts with 'self signed certificate' (reproduced 2026-10-02), and http::fetch_bytes offers neither an insecure mode nor a test-CA hook. Fixture certificates can still be minted with openssl through process::run. S03's TLS-carried assertions do not depend on the transport (the same checks hold over plain HTTP); the lone TLS-native assertion, correct serving behind a TLS listener, would shrink to proving the listener binds.
